walkthroughs.title: Get started with Oracle SQL Developer Extension for VS Code
walkthroughs.description: Start by creating a new database connection

steps.title: Navigate to SQL Developer extension
steps.description: Click on the extension icon in the sidebar to get started.

steps.title: Create new database connection
steps.description:
Create a new database connection by expanding the **CONNECTIONS** dropdown, and click Create Connection.
[Create Connection](command:sqldeveloper.walkthroughs.createConnection)

steps.title: Test, connect, and save connection
steps.description: Once you fill in the credentials, use connection actions to test, connect and save your connection.

steps.title: Next Steps
steps.description:
The SQL Worksheet allows you to run queries and scripts, and offers code insight, snippets, drag and drop support to help speed up writing SQL.
[Discover SQL Worksheet](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%22Oracle.sql-developer%23sqldeveloper.walkthroughs.worksheet%22)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Oracle SQL Developer Extension for VS Code

steps.title: Open a SQL worksheet
steps.description:
You can open a worksheet using **Open SQL Worksheet** icon in your active connection.
[Open SQL Worksheet](command:sqldeveloper.walkthroughs.openWorksheet)

steps.title: Attach/Detach Connection
steps.description: Associate or de-associate a connection to a worksheet by clicking the fifth icon in the top right of your worksheet or the status bar item in the bottom right.

steps.title: Run Statement
steps.description: Once the worksheet opened you can execute easily your SQL statements by clicking the first icon in the top right of your worksheet.

steps.title: Run Script
steps.description: Run your SQL statements and get the output as script by clicking the second icon in the top right of your worksheet.

steps.title: Run in SQLcl
steps.description: Run your SQL statements in SQLcl using the the third icon in the toolbar or by using the associated keyboard shortcut.

steps.title: Explain plan
steps.description: Displays an execution plan for a SQL statement by clicking the forth icon in the top right of your worksheet.

steps.title: Review your executed statements
steps.description:
At any time, you can click on the **SQL HISTORY** tab of bottom panel, to review a history of the statements you have executed.

💡 You can drag and drop or double-click any statement and it will be inserted into the worksheet.

steps.title: Next Steps
steps.description:
Start working with your data by leveraging our database object features.
[Explore database object features](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%22Oracle.sql-developer%23sqldeveloper.walkthroughs.databaseObjects%22)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Oracle SQL Developer Extension for VS Code

steps.title: Create a new table
steps.description: You can create a table by executing CREATE statements in the SQL worksheet.

media.altText: visually inspecting new tables under connections dropdown

steps.title: Access and manipulate your data
steps.description:
You can visually inspect your tables by navigating to **CONNECTIONS**, choosing the appropriate connection, and navigating to Tables.
Then you can add data to your table by utilizing the Insert button.
When it comes to updating data, a quick click on a row enables easy editing, and then you can commit your changes.

steps.title: Create PL/SQL objects
steps.description: Similar to tables you can create your PL/SQL objects by executing a PL/SQL code in the SQL worksheet.

steps.title: Execute PL/SQL
steps.description: You can execute your PL/SQL objects by clicking on Run button and you will see that your PL/SQL objects are successfully completed.
